title: Sonny and the Full Moon | Bedtime Story
description: On the night of the full moon, Sonny the little quokka discovers that the familiar bush has turned completely magical — glowing silver and new — before she settles into the most beautiful sleep. A luminous bedtime story from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales, perfect for winding down at the end of the day.
narration:
Tonight was different. Sunny could feel it before she even opened her eyes.

She padded out of her little sleeping place and looked up through the gum trees — and there it was. The full moon. Big and round and impossibly bright, hanging right in the middle of the sky like a lantern that belonged to the whole bush.

Sunny set off along the path she knew so well. But tonight, everything looked completely different.

The silver light turned the old gum tree trunks into something like pale silver columns. The fallen log by the creek — the one she passed every single day — was draped in moonlight and looked like something from a dream. Even the grass, the ordinary everyday grass, shimmered softly as though tiny stars had settled on every blade.

Sunny walked slowly, turning her head this way and that, taking it all in. The bush she had always known had become something magical, just by the light of one very full moon.

And then she found it. Her favourite sleeping spot — the small hollow at the foot of the big old banksia tree, lined with dry leaves and soft bark. She had slept there a hundred times. But tonight, in the full moon light, it looked like the most beautiful place in the whole world. Silvery and warm and perfectly hers.

Sunny turned around once, slowly, and curled herself into a small round shape among the leaves.

Above her, through the wide banksia branches, the moon shone on. It watched over the whole sleeping bush. And it watched over Sunny, too — round and peaceful and still.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, full moon. Goodnight, little one.
